captions.linkedin:
Stop chasing high-growth narratives. Fama and French ran 50 years of US equity data and found that robust operating profitability beat weak operating profitability with a t-statistic of 2.92.

The signal isn't earnings. It isn't revenue. It's operating profit divided by book equity, lagged cleanly.

Here's the complete logic from JFE 2015. No black box:

🔹 OP METRIC. Operating profitability = (revenue minus COGS minus SG&A minus interest) divided by book equity.
🔹 SIZE-NEUTRAL SORT. Robust and weak split independently of market cap, so small-caps don't carry the factor alone.
🔹 ANNUAL FORMATION. Rebalance end of June using prior fiscal-year data.
🔹 VALUE-WEIGHTED. Positions sized by market cap inside 6 intersection portfolios.
🔹 LONG-SHORT. Long high-profitability firms, short low-profitability firms.

Fama and French 2015, in-sample through December 2013. Small-stock RMW (t=3.06) drives the factor. Big-cap RMW is weak (t=1.81). Post-publication decay documented. You verify it.
